description: GPU Collatz verification suffers from warp divergence because different starting numbers require different iteration counts. Angeltveit mitigates this by grouping 2^16 values with the same f (odd-step count) into a single kernel, ensuring similar workloads per thread. Barina batches intervals of 2^40 numbers instead.
mathematical_formalization: Warp efficiency = (active_threads * cycles_used) / (warp_size * total_cycles). For uniform f, E[survivors|f] ~ C * density(BV_i), and iteration count in Step 3 ~ proportional to f. Grouping by f minimizes variance within warps.
analogical_connections: Work-stealing in Cilk — balance heterogeneous tasks across workers
Packet classification in routers — group flows by prefix length
Batch normalization in neural networks — normalize within batch for stability
implementation_hypothesis: Sort recursive step outputs by f value. Launch one CUDA kernel per f-group of 2^16 values. Each thread processes one n_0, applies BV_i sieve, then iterates Step 3 for survivors. Use shared memory for the bitvector segment.
experiment_seed: Compare sequential intervals vs f-grouped dispatch vs dynamic work-stealing. Measure warp efficiency and throughput.
